newsitem.title: IRAQ: First medicines under oil deal arrive in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: First medicines under oil deal arrive in Iraq.

text.p: Iraq has received the first shipment of medical supplies under its oil-for-food deal with the United Nations, Iraqi newspapers said on Saturday.
The papers, quoting a Health Ministry source, said four trucks carrying 61.5 tonnes of medicine had reached Iraq and several more were expected in a few days.

Under the deal, which went into effect in December, Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy urgent needs for Iraqis, suffering from U.N. sanctions imposed for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Baghdad has often complained about delays in the arrival of medical supplies. Food bought under the pact has been piling up in Iraq and the government distributed the first food rations this month.

Health Minister Umeed Madhat Mubarak said on Friday in Geneva, where he attended a meeting of the World Health Organisation, that despite the deal "not a single tablet" had reached the country, although some 550 contracts were signed with foreign firms.

Earlier this week, U.N. Under-Secretary General Yasushi Akashi told reporters in Baghdad at the end of a visit to Iraq that the country's humanitarian problems remained serious and conditions in hospitals were deplorable.
